They were absolute variances in the predictors' own units, so the decision changed with the predictors' scale and not with anything the arithmetic could resolve. The decision is now the quadrature's own. The 2-D rule runs exactly when its zero-jitter Cholesky pivots, a and b - (c/sqrt(a))^2, formed with the same operations as cholesky_static, are both positive. Any other covariance is rank one in floating point, or indefinite. The nearest positive semidefinite covariance keeps only its major eigenpair, m + r with m = (a+b)/2 and r = hypot((a-b)/2, c), and the 1-D rule integrates along the major eigenvector. No positive eigenvalue means a point mass. A non-finite covariance is now refused. Before, f64::max turned a NaN variance into 0, and a NaN cross term made every Cholesky retry fail, so the helper silently returned the integrand at the mean.

reason: #2469: THETA_EFF_MAX (1e9) was a picked effective-dispersion threshold above which the estimation-widened Poisson count interval switched from the negative-binomial surrogate to the exact Poisson quantile. The NB surrogate reaches the Poisson only through prob = theta/(theta+mu). statrs' beta_reg, behind negative_binomial_quantile, forms the complement mu/(theta+mu) by rounding, so the NB CDF carries relative error of order u*theta/mu, while the widening the surrogate adds is of order mu/theta. The switch now sits where those two cross, theta_eff > mu/sqrt(u), with u = gam_linalg::roundoff::UNIT_ROUNDOFF. For mu = 10 that is about 9.5e8, so the picked number was of the right order but independent of mu.

reason: #2469: LOGIT_SIGMA_DEGENERATE (1e-10) was the picked sigma below which the integrated logistic expectation returns the point-mass limit sigmoid(mu) and its derivative. The cloglog twin CLOGLOG_SIGMA_DEGENERATE is unchanged: for S = exp(-e^mu), |S''/S| grows like e^(2mu), so no mu-uniform switch exists there.
